title: Senior's toolkit: integration testing
summary: WebApplicationFactory and ConfigureTestServices, Testcontainers for real databases, Respawn for clean tables, and Verify for snapshot and contract tests.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: integration tests
steps.body: The libraries behind most .NET integration suites, and the calls you use from them.

toolkit.what: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing: start the real Program.cs on a TestServer. Share it with IClassFixture; customise per test with WithWebHostBuilder.
flags: an HttpClient wired to the in-memory server
replace services after the app registered its own
in Program.cs, so tests can name the entry point

toolkit.what: Testcontainers for .NET: start a throwaway PostgreSQL (or SQL Server, Redis, RabbitMQ...) in Docker for the test run. Needs a running Docker.
flags: hand it to the app or DbContext
pin the same version as production
removed after the run (and by the Ryuk reaper if the run crashes)

toolkit.what: Respawn: delete the data in every table (in foreign-key order) between tests, much faster than recreating the database.
flags: keep reference data and the migrations table

toolkit.what: Verify (Verify.XunitV3, Verify.Http): snapshot an object, a JSON body or a whole HTTP response, with dates and GUIDs scrubbed, and diff it against the approved file.
flags: remove values that change every run
committed: the contract other teams rely on

steps.prompt: Match each problem to the tool.
pairs: the real payment client must not be called from tests
tests share one database and see each other's rows
the mobile team depends on the exact JSON shape
a Verify snapshot of the response

steps.prompt: CI agents have no Docker, but some integration tests use Testcontainers. What do experienced teams do?
options: Mark those tests with a trait (Category=Container) and run them in a pipeline job that has Docker; the fast job filters them out
Replace PostgreSQL with the EF InMemory provider
Catch the Docker exception and pass the test
steps.explain: Split by trait and run each slice where it can run. A test that silently passes when its dependency is missing is worse than no test.
